doc_screened_files.reason: Most directly related to the panic site: its docs explicitly mention synthesizing generics for delegation items and handling inherited parameters, which matches `inherit_sig_for_delegation_item` failing while building a delegation signature.

Delegation signature inheritance also depends on collecting inherited predicates; this file explicitly handles inherited predicates for delegation items, so a missed bound here could leave the synthesized signature incomplete and trigger the unwrap failure.

The reproducer and diagnostics hinge on the lifetime `'a` being out of scope, so binder/lifetime resolution is a strong suspect; this file classifies and resolves bound variables and captures, which is exactly where an undeclared lifetime could be lost for delegation-related signatures.

Delegation items need a computed item type/return type to inherit correctly, and this file owns `type_of` for collected HIR owners and opaque/anonymous const type computation, making it a plausible source of the missing signature information that later caused `suggest_missing_return_type` to run.

This is the collection entry point that feeds delegation metadata into later analysis, so regressions in delegation item collection or item-context wiring here can cascade into an incomplete signature and the downstream unwrap panic.

The bug involves a delegation item with generic/lifetime arguments, and this file lowers and validates generic argument lists; a mismatch between collected delegation generics and lowered generics could explain the missing `'a` or absent associated item data.

Delegation signature reconstruction relies on HIR-to-`ty` lowering of types and binders, and this module is the central lowering interface for those conversions, so it is a likely shared dependency for the faulty delegation path.

The query stack shows the panic surfacing during body type checking after delegation setup; this file runs the main body checks and is the point where the missing return-type information was detected and fed into the failing suggestion path.

The stack trace shows `FnCtxt::suggest_missing_return_type` immediately before the panic, and this module owns the per-body type-checking context and that suggestion machinery, so it is a strong downstream site for the `None`-driven crash.

As the crate root wiring collection, delegation, checking, and lowering together, this is a plausible integration point if the delegation pipeline is assembling incomplete state across those phases rather than a single isolated helper being wrong.
